bindings.description: Contested alleged subletting of premises originally let to Onkar Nath. The appellant alleges post-9-June-1952 unauthorized subletting; the respondent invokes pre-existing occupation by Kirori Mal and Dewan Chand Gupta. The prior record also refers to two subtenants through whom other persons claimed rights. These accounts are retained together without presuming that all mentioned occupants or transactions are identical.

bindings.identity_reason: The appellant's allegation internally identifies an alleged post-9-June-1952 subletting without written consent concerning the tenancy of Onkar Nath and the identified Delhi building. That allegation supplies an identifiable focal pleading relationship. However, the respondent's account concerns Kirori Mal and Dewan Chand Gupta occupying the premises before Onkar Nath's tenancy, while the later passage describes other persons claiming rights through two earlier subtenants. The record does not establish that the named occupants, the predecessor pair and the recipients of the appellant's alleged disposition are identical or involved in one transaction. Accordingly, complete cross-account identity remains unresolved, but the allegation's internal association and the established tenancy and building identities must not be discarded.

bindings.scope_reason: The restored account identifies premises in Delhi and a dispute expressly framed around alleged subletting after 9 June 1952 without written consent. The prior Rent Controller passage also refers to an alleged violation of section 14(1)(b). The statutory framework therefore corresponds to the supplied subject matter and jurisdictional setting. Whether an identified occupation predates the tenancy, whether the tenant subsequently made a disposition, whether the alleged recipients are the same persons and whether the relevant consent was written are transaction-specific identity or substantive-test questions. They do not render the whole statutory framework incompatible. The precise historical availability of the supplied interpretive opinion remains qualified separately.

reviewed_join_limits.reason: The appellant's pleaded post-1952 allegation links conduct, timing and the identified building within one asserted arrangement. The named occupants in the respondent's account are described as occupying the premises before Onkar Nath's tenancy. The supplied passages do not establish that these persons were recipients of the appellant's alleged later disposition or identify the same specific part of the building. Consequently, the respondent's earlier-occupation account cannot automatically be merged into the appellant's alleged transaction for date, subtenancy-incident or part-specific premises evaluation. bindings.dependency_review_reason: The previous UNRESOLVED identity assessment is retained because the record contains genuinely uncertain connections among the alleged later disposition, named pre-existing occupants and an incompletely identified predecessor pair. This does not justify a blanket refusal to join propositions explicitly contained within the appellant's single allegation or to preserve the identified tenant and building. The broad identity gate is therefore replaced with transaction-specific BINDING limits. Scope is revised to COMPATIBLE because the Delhi section 14(1)(b) framework is expressly implicated. The distinction between allegations, prior findings, relative chronology, tenant-caused disposition and written consent remains governed by the existing restrictions. Uncertain interpretation timing remains localized to the opinion-derived tests. No source-established relationship is extended to an unsupported person or transaction, and no substantive test or claim outcome is decided.

coverage_limits: The appellant's account of a post-1952 unauthorized subletting and the respondent's earlier-occupation account remain competing positions, not separately proven transactions.
The named tenant and building are identified through restored source text.
The identity of Kirori Mal and Dewan Chand Gupta relative to the earlier unnamed subtenant pair is unresolved.
Earlier physical occupation cannot automatically be converted into tenant-caused divestment or retained legal possession.
The reported landlord consent has unspecified form and cannot independently resolve written consent.
The rent note is described by the respondent and was not independently inspected.
The supplied facts do not establish assignment, retained legal possession, or the detailed incidents required for subletting.
No burden allocation or proof standard is supplied. No claim outcome or test label is predicted.
